To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Brisbane brand is not a coherent brand but a collection of sub-brands, that these sub-brands are not aligned with the destination's brand promise, and that the destination's brand equity has been eroded by the lack of a collaborative environment that would enable stakeholders to work together to build a strong destination brand.
The city of Brisbane, Australia has developed its destination brand through the use of an integrated marketing communications campaign that is focused on the city's river.
the destination brand of the city of Brisbane is a complex construct that is the outcome of a process that involves a large number of stakeholders.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of destination brands in a context of complex and dynamic interorganizational relationships that characterize tourism destinations and the development of a brand identity in a context of conflicting organizational interests.
the development of a collaborative environment that is necessary to build destination brand equity in the case of a tourism destination.
the following questions: What is the role of the destination brand?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

tourism destinations are complex systems, in that they are composed of many interdependent parts, each of which contributes in its own way to the overall functioning of the destination (Laws et al., 2002; Poon, 2000).

the development of a successful destination brand is dependent on the development of a collaborative and integrated environment among all the stakeholders in the destination (Gnoth, 2002; Gnoth and Zins, 2010).

tourism destinations are characterized by a complex set of stakeholders that are involved in the delivery of a tourism product and that the destination brand is a reflection of the sum total of the individual brands of each of the stakeholders.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the city has a strong brand but it is not a tourism brand.

the destination branding process is not only a matter of creating a brand for the destination but rather a matter of managing the destination brand as the sum of all the brands that are associated to the destination.
we have identified the need for a collaborative environment among stakeholders, and the lack of such environment in Brisbane.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the destination brand is a social construction that emerges from a complex set of interactions among the stakeholders in the destination.

the tourism destination brand should be developed as a collaborative effort among stakeholders and that the destination image is a complex construct that should be considered from multiple perspectives and in the context of the different target markets.

destination brands are not the result of the work of a single entity but the result of the collaboration of a number of stakeholders, and the success of destination branding initiatives is dependent on the ability of these stakeholders to work together.
